justification: Single published-stat correction (dcpSetbackTripleCouncils: 24 -> 23) in frontend-nextjs/lib/coverage.ts, the project's own designated single source of truth for public-facing coverage numbers. No served logic changes, no schema, no query changes -- corrects an exact-count field that had drifted from the live database, caught by the project's own data-watch workflow.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: any exact-count field in COVERAGE disagrees with a fresh live query against production.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before this change: 'Councils w/ front+side+rear setback  24  23  DRIFT', 'DRIFT DETECTED'. Independently re-derived the live count myself (not just trusting the script) via a fresh read-only session against the documented query in the file's own header -- confirmed 23, and listed the 5 councils currently missing at least one control type (burwood, cumberland, ku_ring_gai, parramatta, woollahra). After the fix: 'Councils w/ front+side+rear setback  23  23  OK', 'All DB-backed coverage stats are current.'

pre_impl.existing_data: dcp_setback_controls, grouped by lga, filtered WHERE is_current AND (needs_review IS NULL OR needs_review=FALSE) AND lga NOT IN ('nsw_statewide','inner_west') -- the exact query already documented in coverage.ts's own header, re-run read-only via scripts/dq_db.py.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Did not assume the script's DRIFT report was correct without re-deriving it independently -- ran the identical query myself in a separate session and got the same 23, plus enumerated which 5 councils lack full triple coverage (not identified by the script, added here as context though the specific council that dropped from the prior 24 was not traced).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Corrects the existing published figure to match current live state; does not change the query, the threshold, or any other field in the same file. Other fields in this file use a rounded-DOWN '+' display form specifically so growth doesn't cause drift -- this is the one exact-count field, which is why it alone triggered DRIFT.

values.read_at: frontend-nextjs/app/for/conveyancers/page.tsx:59 (the only consumer found via grep of app/ and components/ for this constant)

queries.purpose: re-derive the published stat independently against live production before changing it
queries.file_line: documented in frontend-nextjs/lib/coverage.ts header, re-run via scripts/dq_db.py session
queries.where_clause: dcp_setback_controls WHERE is_current AND (needs_review IS NULL OR needs_review=FALSE) AND lga NOT IN ('nsw_statewide','inner_west'), GROUP BY lga, count councils with all three of front/side/rear setback types present
queries.if_zero: would mean zero councils have full triple coverage -- not the case, 23 do
queries.if_wrong: matched scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py's own independently-computed figure exactly (23), corroborating both

break_it.scenario: The published figure is corrected downward without checking whether other fields in the same file also drifted, leaving other overstatements live.
break_it.what_happens: Other exact-count claims could still be wrong.
break_it.how: Ran the full verify_coverage_stats.py script, not just the one failing field -- every other field reported OK against a fresh live query in the same run.
break_it.repro: python scripts/verify_coverage_stats.py output shows all 9 stats, only the one field flagged

post_merge.manual_verify: None needed beyond the falsifiable check already run -- this is a pure display-value correction with no runtime branch depending on the specific number.
